cards.title: Use explicit no-pressure language for genuinely low-commitment offers
cards.summary: For a free resource or trial, clearly state the real follow-up and obligation terms so shoppers do not assume a hidden sales commitment.
cards.use_when: Writing copy for an email sign-up incentive, product quiz result, back-in-stock alert, sample request, free guide, or trial where customers may fear unwanted contact.

cards.title: Stack credible bonuses and prove their stated value
cards.summary: Multiple bonuses can make a bundle more compelling when each is useful, clearly valued, and available at the stated price outside the promotion.
cards.use_when: Building a product bundle, subscription acquisition offer, digital companion pack, or purchase-threshold promotion.

cards.title: Use first-order and completion rewards to drive repeat purchase
cards.summary: A bonus can either lower the risk of a first order or reward customers for completing a defined replenishment or collection journey.
cards.use_when: Designing a subscription launch, replenishment program, collectible series, loyalty milestone, or first-purchase acquisition offer.

cards.title: Treat classic direct-response offer mechanics as test hypotheses
cards.summary: Older direct-marketing rules of thumb can suggest offer tests, but a store should evaluate them on contribution margin, repeat purchasing, and refunds rather than response alone.
cards.use_when: Prioritizing experiments on payment terms, subscription structure, bonuses, discounts, or deferred-payment options for an ecommerce offer.

cards.title: Test price with positioning, not as an isolated lower-is-better choice
cards.summary: A low price can signal insufficient quality to a professional or high-intent segment, so test price alongside the audience and value proposition it communicates.
cards.use_when: Repositioning a product for a premium customer segment, deciding whether to introduce a higher-priced version, or diagnosing stalled sales at a low price point.

cards.title: Frame fixed savings in dollars and variable savings in percentages
cards.summary: When every eligible shopper receives the same monetary saving, a dollar-off message may be more concrete than the equivalent percentage; test the framing on your own catalog.
cards.use_when: Writing sale banners, email subject lines, coupon messages, or product-page promotions with an equivalent dollar-off and percentage-off expression.

cards.title: Make a lump-sum price easier to evaluate with truthful per-use math
cards.summary: For products or subscriptions used over a known period, per-day or per-use framing can contextualize the price without hiding the actual amount due.
cards.use_when: Merchandising annual subscriptions, replenishment plans, durable goods, multi-month supply bundles, or higher-ticket products on a PDP or landing page.

cards.title: Anchor price against real alternatives that solve the same customer problem
cards.summary: Price becomes easier to accept when shoppers first see the credible cost, effort, or risk of alternative ways to achieve the same outcome.
cards.use_when: Writing a PDP, bundle page, comparison table, or acquisition landing page for a product whose price needs context.

cards.title: Test installment and trial offers on collected revenue, not first-payment conversion
cards.summary: A lower initial payment or trial can reduce entry friction, but it must be evaluated against cancellations, payment failures, returns, and total cash collected.
cards.use_when: Setting payment options for a high-ticket product, prepaid replenishment plan, subscription, or a product that requires a paid trial before a customer can assess fit.

cards.title: Use good-better-best bundles to give shoppers a clear value ladder
cards.summary: Three well-differentiated purchase options can raise order value by making the middle or best-value bundle easier to choose without removing a basic entry option.
cards.use_when: Creating product bundles, multi-packs, replenishment quantities, subscription plan tiers, or a pricing table for a core product line.

cards.title: Design guarantees through four operational decisions
cards.summary: A guarantee needs clear choices about duration, conditions, covered costs, and refund activation so it lowers purchase risk without creating avoidable ambiguity.
cards.use_when: Creating or revising a return guarantee for physical goods, consumables, durable products, or digital products on a PDP and in store policies.

cards.title: Make the guarantee visible and simple at the purchase decision
cards.summary: A guarantee only reduces purchase anxiety if shoppers can notice, understand, and trust it before adding the product to cart.
cards.use_when: Laying out a product page, bundle page, cart drawer, checkout reassurance area, or promotional email for a product with a meaningful return policy.

cards.title: Consider keep-the-download refunds for low-abuse digital products
cards.summary: For non-returnable digital goods, openly allowing a refund while the buyer keeps the file can reduce perceived risk, provided the merchant monitors abuse and economics.
cards.use_when: Selling ebooks, templates, printables, downloadable guides, digital patterns, or similar files that cannot practically be recovered after delivery.

cards.title: Use real deadlines and credible inventory scarcity
cards.summary: Urgency works when a sale end date or stock limit is operationally true, communicated consistently, and actually enforced.
cards.use_when: Planning a seasonal promotion, product drop, limited-edition launch, preorder, email campaign, cart promotion, or low-stock PDP message.

cards.title: Select purchase bonuses differently from lead-capture incentives
cards.summary: For a purchase offer, desirability can be the main bonus criterion; for email acquisition, relevance often matters more because unrelated gifts can attract low-intent freebie seekers.
cards.use_when: Choosing between a gift-with-purchase, an email sign-up incentive, a B2B sample offer, or a corporate buying promotion.

cards.title: Choose premiums that fit the buyer and the product
cards.summary: Use a product-related premium or discount that helps the buyer justify the purchase, rather than an unrelated giveaway that attracts low-intent responders.
cards.use_when: Designing a first-order bonus, email-capture incentive, wholesale promotion, or product-launch offer for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Use samples and evaluations to prove fit before purchase
cards.summary: Let shoppers test the product on their own need, material, or configuration when generic product claims cannot establish fit.
cards.use_when: Selling configurable, technical, high-consideration, or sensory products online where a shopper needs evidence before committing to a full purchase.

cards.title: Design trials to overcome non-use, not just purchase risk
cards.summary: A no-obligation trial needs a defined evaluation window, easy return terms, and activation reminders so customers actually use the product before deciding.
cards.use_when: Creating a try-before-you-buy, subscription trial, product-rental, or introductory-use offer for an ecommerce product whose value becomes clear through use.

cards.title: Use a loss leader only with a credible back-end plan
cards.summary: A low- or no-margin first purchase can acquire customers, but it works only when the product is genuinely valuable and follow-on economics support the acquisition cost.
cards.use_when: Pricing an entry product, starter kit, paid sample, or affiliate offer intended to acquire new ecommerce customers rather than generate first-order profit.

cards.title: Give an unusually strong offer headline-level prominence
cards.summary: Place standard offers near the conversion point, but feature a genuinely exceptional offer in the headline or above the fold when it resolves the shopper’s main hesitation.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a promotion, PDP, category page, paid-ad landing page, or email should lead with the offer or with the product’s primary benefit.

cards.title: Focus ecommerce copy work on the high-leverage decision points
cards.summary: Prioritize the hero message, central positioning, and offer language over minor stylistic edits when improving a product or campaign page.
cards.use_when: Allocating copywriting and design-review time for a PDP, collection page, landing page, email, or checkout promotion.

cards.title: Reduce checkout friction while preserving attribution
cards.summary: Make ecommerce forms short and usable, show critical terms and bonuses clearly, and use campaign-specific tracking to identify the offer and creative that produced each order.
cards.use_when: Auditing checkout, a lead-capture form, or a campaign landing page that is losing shoppers before they submit or buy.

cards.title: Test offer variables with message-matched landing pages
cards.summary: Use controlled A/B tests to choose among offers, prices, headlines, bonuses, guarantees, and page treatments, while keeping the acquisition message consistent with the destination page.
cards.use_when: Choosing between competing ecommerce promotions or diagnosing a landing page, PDP, or acquisition campaign with weak conversion.

cards.title: Build a risk-reversing offer with a tested guarantee and deadline
cards.summary: Combine a clear related premium, an understandable guarantee, and legitimate urgency to make the purchase feel safer and more timely, then test the terms against margin and returns.
cards.use_when: Creating or auditing a product-launch, seasonal, bundle, cart, or checkout offer where shoppers hesitate over risk, timing, or value.

cards.title: Offer vs. discount: test structure, not depth
cards.summary: An offer is a stack of benefits and terms; swapping 10/20/30% off is only discount testing and rarely breaks a revenue ceiling.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to test next on your store's acquisition offer when discount-depth tests keep producing flat or temporary lifts.

cards.title: Front-loaded subscription discount formula
cards.summary: Give a large first-order discount and a small recurring one, because a flat recurring discount doesn't create urgency to subscribe now.
cards.use_when: Designing or reworking subscribe-and-save terms for a consumable product to lift first-order subscription opt-ins without permanently thinning margin.

cards.title: Strategic welcome kit gifts that improve product use
cards.summary: Free gifts should help the customer consume the core product better, not be unrelated branded swag.
cards.use_when: Selecting the free gift or welcome-kit contents for a subscription or first-order offer on a consumable product.

cards.title: Four subscription offer models, ranked
cards.summary: From flat recurring discount to discount-plus-welcome-kit to subscription-only, the source ranks kit-based stacked offers as the strongest.
cards.use_when: Choosing which subscription offer architecture to run for a given brand and customer.

cards.title: Raise list price, then discount to target
cards.summary: Fund a rich stacked offer by pricing higher and discounting down, so the visible discount is large relative to a high anchor.
cards.use_when: Structuring pricing and discount depth together so a stacked offer (gifts, credit, deep first-order discount) still protects net revenue.

cards.title: Middle-option anchoring on bundles
cards.summary: Auto-select the middle bundle and price it against the single-unit price so the bundle becomes the default baseline.
cards.use_when: Designing bundle tiers and default selection on a PDP or bundle landing page for apparel, accessories, or repeat-purchase goods.

cards.title: Bundle the same product, not a mixed assortment
cards.summary: Same-SKU bundles (more units, different flavor or color) outperform cross-category assortments because buyers don't want to be forced into items they don't want.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to bundle for a supplement, consumable, or multi-variant product line.

cards.title: Frame bundles as 'free' rather than percent off
cards.summary: 'Buy 2 get 1 free' beats the mathematically equivalent '33% off 3' because free outperforms a percentage in the customer's mind.
cards.use_when: Choosing the copy and framing for a multi-unit bundle offer.

cards.title: Anchor free gift by consumption value
cards.summary: Free gift offers convert, but the source's data shows $25 in store credit beat a generic free gift by roughly 3x on opt-ins and placed-order rate.
cards.use_when: Choosing between a free gift and a cash-equivalent first-order offer in a pop-up or welcome offer.

cards.title: Dollar-off vs percent-off by AOV threshold
cards.summary: Above roughly $100 AOV, dollar-off reads bigger; below $100, percent-off reads bigger.
cards.use_when: Writing the headline for a pop-up, first-order offer, or site-wide discount.

cards.title: Stack site-wide offers into one advertised first-order value
cards.summary: Combine your evergreen site discount with the welcome code and advertise the aggregate, so the headline reads as one large dollar figure.
cards.use_when: Writing the pop-up and welcome-flow messaging for a store that already runs a permanent site or subscription discount.

cards.title: Mystery discount framing
cards.summary: A hidden-value framing ('mystery offer') lifts opt-in because curiosity is added on top of the discount itself.
cards.use_when: Writing pop-up copy to increase email/SMS list opt-in rate, especially when you're not willing to increase discount depth.

cards.title: What not to run as a first-order offer
cards.summary: The source limits first-order offers to dollar off, percent off, free gift/BOGO, and cash back — and warns against giveaways and free guides.
cards.use_when: Shortlisting the first-order and pop-up offer types when building a lead-capture or acquisition campaign.

cards.title: Measure offers on 90-day LTV, not first order alone
cards.summary: An offer that wins the first purchase can hurt repeat rate, so measure opt-in, placed-order, first-order revenue, and 90-day downstream value.
cards.use_when: Reading the results of a pop-up, first-order, or subscription offer test before rolling it out.

cards.title: Segment measurement by subscriber status
cards.summary: Comparing subscriber vs non-subscriber cohort LTV at six months shows why subscription conversion should be pushed on the first order.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much of the first-order offer budget to spend on pushing subscription rather than one-time purchase.

cards.title: Everyday offer plus a flash deals page for urgency
cards.summary: Keep bundles as the evergreen core offer and route urgency ads to a separate limited-time page to convert price-sensitive and overstock buyers.
cards.use_when: Planning merchandising and promo calendar for an apparel or accessory store already running an evergreen bundle.

cards.title: Research competitor pop-up offers for framing variants
cards.summary: Collect live pop-ups from brands across your space to generate framing variants beyond the plain percent-off.
cards.use_when: Building a backlog of pop-up and first-order offer variants to test.

cards.title: Three Ways to Trade Unit Margin
cards.summary: Frame every offer as trading unit margin for conversion rate, AOV, or repeat purchases/LTV.
cards.use_when: Choosing what kind of offer to run on a store before defaulting to a plain discount

cards.title: The $14 Sock Problem: Free Shipping on Low-AOV Items
cards.summary: Free shipping on a low-AOV single item can raise conversion rate while reducing net profit because the brand absorbs shipping with no offsetting cart volume.
cards.use_when: Evaluating whether to add free shipping or a small discount to a single low-price product

cards.title: Multi-Pack Tier Bundling to Fix AOV and ROAS
cards.summary: Discount a multi-pack instead of the single unit so the customer pays less per unit while the brand earns more per order.
cards.use_when: The store sells one hero SKU and first-order AOV is too low to cover acquisition cost

cards.title: Auto-Select the Middle Bundle Option
cards.summary: Anchor a three-tier bundle so the middle option is pre-selected and priced against the single unit, making the bundle the baseline.
cards.use_when: Designing bundle or multi-pack tiers on a PDP

cards.title: Volume Thresholds and Cart Incentives
cards.summary: Discount on crossing a spend threshold so the customer saves while the brand increases order value.
cards.use_when: Designing cart-level incentives or checkout upsells to lift AOV

cards.title: Mystery Discount Pop-Up to Lift Opt-In Rate
cards.summary: Replace a static 10% off pop-up with an interactive mystery discount to roughly double opt-in rate while offering the same discount.
cards.use_when: Setting up welcome pop-ups and email/SMS capture offers

cards.title: Dollar Off vs Percent Off by AOV
cards.summary: Use dollar-off framing when AOV is above $100 and percent-off framing when AOV is below $100.
cards.use_when: Writing the headline discount for a pop-up, welcome code, or promotion

cards.title: Front-Loaded Subscription Discount Structure
cards.summary: Use a large first-order discount plus a small recurring discount to incentivize subscription opt-in without destroying long-term margin.
cards.use_when: Setting the discount structure for a subscribe-and-save offer

cards.title: LTV Ceiling Sets Your Max CAC
cards.summary: Your subscription LTV determines the maximum you can pay to acquire a customer, letting you outbid single-purchase competitors.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much you can spend on ads for a subscription or repeat-purchase product

cards.title: Welcome Kit and Gift Criteria
cards.summary: Free gifts should deepen use of the core product, not add unrelated swag.
cards.use_when: Designing subscription welcome kits, order bumps, or gift-with-purchase offers

cards.title: Zero-COGS Digital Bonus Stacking
cards.summary: Add digital companions with no incremental COGS to raise perceived value for physical products.
cards.use_when: Building perceived value into a physical product offer without discounting further

cards.title: Risk Reversal and Guarantee Tiers
cards.summary: Layer a standard money-back guarantee with optional delayed-capture billing to remove purchase risk.
cards.use_when: Designing guarantees, returns policy, or a try-before-you-buy offer on a PDP

cards.title: Scarcity and Urgency Implementation
cards.summary: Use live stock states, time-gated deals, and drop models to create honest urgency.
cards.use_when: Planning promotions, limited releases, or on-site urgency mechanics

cards.title: Outcome-Driven Product Naming
cards.summary: Name products for the outcome they deliver instead of generic categorization.
cards.use_when: Naming or renaming SKUs, bundles, or landing page headings

cards.title: Order Bumps, One-Click Upsells, and Gift-with-Purchase
cards.summary: Prioritize free or cheap conversion levers like one-click upsells, order bumps, and gifts with purchase before spending margin on deeper discounts.
cards.use_when: Deciding which offer mechanics to add first to an existing store

cards.title: Prepaid Annuals and Prepaid Multi-Month Plans
cards.summary: Offer a large discount for prepaying multiple months or a year to collect cash and margin up front.
cards.use_when: Designing subscription terms or cash-flow-friendly offers

cards.title: Interactive Spin/Scratch/Quiz Opt-In Mechanics
cards.summary: Interactive reveal mechanics all funnel to the same mystery discount and increase engagement and opt-in rate.
cards.use_when: Choosing which pop-up or capture format to run on-site

cards.title: Comparing Offer Strategies by Boldness
cards.summary: Match offer type to cash position: profitable bundles for cash-tight stores, aggressive first-order losses for well-funded ones.
cards.use_when: Choosing between a bundle-focused growth plan and an aggressive subscription acquisition plan

cards.title: Value Equation Applied to Physical Products
cards.summary: Map the four value equation variables (dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time delay, effort and sacrifice) to concrete ecommerce levers.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing why a product page or offer is not converting and choosing which lever to pull

cards.title: Judge your subscription retention against your product's consumption model
cards.summary: Set realistic churn and LTV targets by classifying your product's natural usage frequency before benchmarking against other brands.
cards.use_when: Setting subscription targets or diagnosing churn and deciding whether your product genuinely supports a subscription offer.

cards.title: Subscription-first offer architecture: no discount on one-time, big discount on sub
cards.summary: Structure the PDP offer so subscription gets the discount and welcome kit while the one-time purchase stays full price, small and discreet.
cards.use_when: Designing or rebuilding the product page offer for a consumable product where you want first-order subscription take rate.

cards.title: Use a 3-option pricing display with two subscription choices
cards.summary: Show three purchase options on the PDP with two of them subscription-based to bias the default toward subscribing.
cards.use_when: Merchandising the buy-box on a subscription PDP to raise first-order take rate.

cards.title: Consumption-focused free gifts to reduce churn
cards.summary: Choose first-order gifts that physically help the customer use the product daily, not generic swag, because the top cancel reason is running out of use-habit.
cards.use_when: Selecting welcome-kit and in-subscription free gifts for a consumable product.

cards.title: Match subscription cadence and quantity to real consumption
cards.summary: Set billing frequency and pack size so customers run out roughly when the next shipment arrives, avoiding 'too much product' cancellations.
cards.use_when: Configuring subscription cadence and quantity options on the PDP or in the portal.

cards.title: Build first-order subscription LTV case with cohort comparison
cards.summary: Compare 6-, 12-, and 24-month LTV of first-order-subscription vs non-subscription buyers to justify investing in take rate.
cards.use_when: Deciding how much offer value to spend to convert first orders into subscriptions, or building the business case internally.

cards.title: Front-load onboarding education in days 1-7 before delivery
cards.summary: Send daily or near-daily education emails in the first week after purchase, timed to the pre-delivery window when cancellation risk is lowest.
cards.use_when: Designing the subscriber onboarding email/SMS sequence after first order.

cards.title: Habit-stacking and long-term pacing messaging
cards.summary: Teach subscribers to attach product use to an existing daily habit and set a 90-120 day results timeline to prevent early cancellation.
cards.use_when: Writing onboarding and ongoing subscriber emails for a daily-use consumable.

cards.title: Optimized billing reminder: lead with delay, bury cancel
cards.summary: Rebuild the pre-charge billing reminder with benefits and education, a prominent one-click delay/skip CTA, and the manage/cancel link at the very bottom.
cards.use_when: Editing the subscription billing reminder email (platform-native or in your ESP).

cards.title: Customize billing reminders by refill number and product
cards.summary: Vary reminder copy by which refill the subscriber is on and which product they hold, especially highlighting upcoming gifts.
cards.use_when: Building segmented billing reminder templates for an active subscription base.

cards.title: Rebuild the order confirmation email off the platform default
cards.summary: Replace the clinical Shopify/native order confirmation with a branded, benefit-led, order-number-aware email to blunt the biggest churn spike.
cards.use_when: Optimizing transactional emails; especially where day-30 churn is high.

cards.title: Exclude active subscribers from standard campaigns
cards.summary: Segment active subscribers out of generic promos and sales, and send them only 1-3 thoughtful campaigns monthly plus exclusive one-time add-on offers.
cards.use_when: Planning campaign sends to a list that includes active subscribers.

cards.title: Cancellation flow: founder splash screen then reason-based branching
cards.summary: Add a founder video splash on the cancel page and route each cancellation reason to a specific save action, targeting a 15%+ save rate.
cards.use_when: Building or tuning the in-portal subscription cancellation flow (e.g., Skio, Recharge).

cards.title: Immediate post-cancel flow plus delayed win-back at 30-60 days
cards.summary: Send one or two reason-specific reactivation emails right after cancellation, then a delayed win-back offer 30-60 days later with an escalated discount.
cards.use_when: Designing email flows for customers who just cancelled a subscription.

cards.title: Treat Subscription Churn as an Acquisition Problem
cards.summary: Shift subscription offer strategy from post-purchase retention tinkering to improving front-end opt-in rate through offer testing.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to allocate subscription budget and effort: subscription acquisition vs. retention/CRM operations.

cards.title: Use Buy More, Save More Instead of Flat Subscribe & Save Discounts
cards.summary: Replace percentage-off Subscribe & Save offers with bulk/tiered quantity offers so you attract value buyers rather than discount hunters.
cards.use_when: Designing or refreshing the subscription offer and pricing ladder on a PDP or dedicated subscription landing page.

cards.title: Map Personas With a Pre-Purchase Quiz and Reallocate Spend by Cohort
cards.summary: Use pre-purchase quiz pop-ups to segment subscribers by goal or identity, then shift ad spend toward the cohorts with better front-end conversion and LTV.
cards.use_when: Deciding audience targeting and acquisition funnel variants for a product whose buyers have distinct goals or identities.

cards.title: Reframe Subscription Ceiling as an Acquisition Problem
cards.summary: Treat subscription growth ceilings as offer/acquisition problems, not retention problems, because retention math hits a hard cap.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to allocate budget and team time between retention programs and acquisition/offer testing for a subscription store.

cards.title: Test Offers to Discover Your Best Subscriber Persona
cards.summary: Use offer testing and personas to learn which use case has the best LTV and lowest churn, not just which converts cheapest.
cards.use_when: When you sell a consumable with multiple use cases (protein powder, turmeric, toothpaste) and want to find the persona segment that retains best before scaling ad spend.

cards.title: Collect Persona Data with Quiz Popups and Post-Purchase Surveys
cards.summary: Segment buyers by goal/identity at purchase using quiz popups, post-purchase surveys, and cancel flows to enable persona-level measurement.
cards.use_when: When you lack quantitative persona data and need a low-effort way to tag subscribers by goal or identity for cohort analysis.
